title: UniFi access point isolated from controller
shortDescription: AP shows 'Isolating' or 'Isolated' status in UniFi controller because it cannot reach a wired uplink with active controller communication.
fullDescription:
When a UniFi mesh AP is wired but the controller stops hearing from it, status flips to 'Isolating' for ~3 minutes then 'Isolated'. The AP keeps serving Wi-Fi clients on its last config but cannot be managed.

Most common cause: a layer-2 issue between the AP and controller - VLAN mismatch, blocked inform port (TCP 8080), or upstream switch problem. Check that AP and controller are in the same management VLAN, or that the AP has the correct inform URL via DHCP option 43.

If the issue persists after L2 verification, factory-reset the AP (hold reset 10 seconds) and re-adopt.

causes.cause: Upstream switch port down or VLAN misassigned

symptoms: AP listed as 'Isolating' or 'Isolated' in controller
Wi-Fi still works but cannot push config

fixSteps.title: Verify uplink
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm switch port is up, correct VLAN, and PoE is delivering 802.3af/at.

fixSteps.title: Test controller reach
fixSteps.instruction: From AP subnet, telnet/curl controller IP on TCP 8080 - must connect.

fixSteps.title: SSH inform URL
fixSteps.instruction: SSH to AP (default ubnt/ubnt or admin password) and run 'set-inform http://<controller>:8080/inform'.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset if stuck
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset button 10s until LED flashes - re-adopt in controller.

whenToCallPro: Engage UI support if AP cannot adopt after factory reset and confirmed L2 reachability.

faq.a: Yes on last applied config; only management is lost.
ubnt/ubnt on factory; otherwise the value set in controller Site settings.

title: UniFi device adoption fails
shortDescription: Controller shows 'Adoption failed' or device stuck in 'Managed by Other' state.
fullDescription:
Adoption failure typically means the AP/switch was previously claimed by a different controller and still trusts those credentials. The fix is a factory reset followed by 'set-inform' to the new controller.

For cloud-keyed devices managed by a UniFi Cloud Key or UDM, the device may also be locked to the cloud account. Remove it from the previous site/cloud account first, then factory reset.

Firmware mismatch can also cause failure - controller may need a manual firmware upgrade for new devices. Use 'upgrade <URL>' over SSH if the controller cannot push automatically.

causes.cause: Device previously adopted to another controller
Firmware too old for current controller version
Bad SSH credentials in Site settings

fixSteps.title: Forget elsewhere
fixSteps.instruction: If managed by another controller/cloud, remove the device from that site first.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset 10 seconds until LED flashes amber/blue.

fixSteps.title: Manual inform
fixSteps.instruction: SSH ubnt/ubnt and run 'set-inform http://<controller>:8080/inform' - run twice if needed.

fixSteps.title: Manual firmware
fixSteps.instruction: If still failing, run 'upgrade <firmware URL>' on the device, then reboot and re-adopt.

whenToCallPro: If device fails to adopt across multiple controllers and resets, RMA via Ubiquiti.
videoSearchQuery: UniFi adoption failed managed by other fix

faq.a: Device thinks another controller owns it - factory reset clears this.

faq.q: Do I need internet to adopt?
faq.a: Helpful for firmware downloads, not strictly required if firmware is current.

title: UniFi LED flashing blue - provisioning
shortDescription: AP LED flashes blue indicating it is currently being provisioned by the controller.
fullDescription:
Flashing blue on a UniFi AP means the device is downloading and applying configuration from the controller. The state should normally last 1-3 minutes after adoption or after a config change.

If it persists longer than 5 minutes, provisioning is stuck. Common causes: failed firmware download (DNS or HTTP issue), low storage on the AP, or controller version mismatch. Check the controller event log for 'provisioning' messages.

Force-provision by selecting the AP in controller and clicking 'Force provision'. If still stuck, factory reset and re-adopt.
symptoms: Event log shows repeated provision attempts

fixSteps.title: Wait 5 minutes
fixSteps.instruction: Provisioning is often slow on first adoption - wait before troubleshooting.

fixSteps.title: Check event log
fixSteps.instruction: In controller, view AP event log for provision errors or firmware download failures.

fixSteps.title: Reset and re-adopt
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset 10s, factory reset, then adopt again.

whenToCallPro: Persistent provisioning loop after factory reset suggests AP hardware fault.
videoSearchQuery: UniFi AP stuck provisioning blue LED

faq.a: No - power loss during firmware flash can brick the AP.
1-3 minutes for config-only, up to 8 minutes if firmware updates.

title: UniFi device offline / disconnected
shortDescription: Device shows 'Disconnected' in controller and is unreachable on the network.
fullDescription:
A 'Disconnected' UniFi device has lost both controller communication and likely network connectivity. Differs from 'Isolated' where wired link still exists. Most likely cause is a power or PoE issue, or a failed cable run.

Check the upstream switch for link state on the AP's port. If the port is down, swap cable, check PoE injector, or move to a known-good port. UniFi APs need 802.3af (15W) or 802.3at (30W) for U6-Pro/Enterprise models.

If link is up but device still disconnected, try connecting a laptop to the same port to test L1/L2.

causes.cause: PoE injector failed or wrong wattage

symptoms: No link light on switch port

fixSteps.title: Inspect AP LED
fixSteps.instruction: If LED is off, suspect power. If steady amber, suspect upgrade in progress.

fixSteps.title: Test PoE injector
fixSteps.instruction: Swap injector or plug AP into a PoE switch port to confirm power delivery.

fixSteps.title: Replace cable
fixSteps.instruction: Test patch cables both at AP and at switch. Use a known-good Cat5e+.

fixSteps.title: Test on different port
fixSteps.instruction: Move AP to a different known-good PoE port to rule out switch port failure.

whenToCallPro: If cable run is in-wall and damaged, hire a low-voltage tech for re-pull.

faq.q: How can I tell if PoE is working?
faq.a: AP LED comes on within 10 seconds of plug-in if PoE is delivering.
Only on legacy UAP models - modern AP6/Enterprise need 802.3af/at.

title: Wi-Fi channel utilization above 80%
shortDescription: UniFi controller flags the AP as having high channel utilization, indicating RF congestion.
fullDescription:
Channel utilization above 80% means the airtime is mostly busy - either by your own clients, neighboring networks, or non-Wi-Fi interference. Throughput drops sharply and clients experience lag.

In UniFi controller, look at AP > RF Environment to see noise floor and overlapping APs. Switch to a less-used channel (DFS channels on 5 GHz often help), reduce 2.4 GHz radio to 20 MHz width, or enable Minimum RSSI to kick weak clients to closer APs.

For dense deployments, reduce TX power and add more APs rather than boosting power - dense low-power is the modern best practice.

causes.cause: Too many clients on a single AP/channel

symptoms: High channel utilization gauge in dashboard

fixSteps.title: Survey RF
fixSteps.instruction: Open AP > RF Environment scan to view nearby SSIDs and channel usage.

fixSteps.title: Pick clear channel
fixSteps.instruction: Set 2.4 GHz to 1, 6, or 11 (20 MHz wide). Set 5 GHz to a lightly used channel including DFS.

fixSteps.title: Adjust TX power
fixSteps.instruction: Set TX power to Medium or Custom to reduce co-channel interference.

fixSteps.title: Add APs if dense
fixSteps.instruction: If >30 clients per AP, add another AP and let band steering balance load.

whenToCallPro: If a wireless site survey is needed, hire a CWNA-certified consultant.

faq.q: Should I use 80 MHz on 5 GHz?
faq.a: In dense areas use 40 MHz - wider channels collide with more neighbors.
Pushes dual-band clients to 5 GHz to free 2.4 GHz.

title: UDM/UXG high CPU from DPI
shortDescription: Dream Machine or UXG runs hot with CPU pinned at 100% caused by Deep Packet Inspection.
fullDescription:
UDM-Pro, UDM-SE, and UXG gateways run DPI to populate the Traffic Identification dashboard and IPS/IDS. On gigabit+ connections this can saturate the CPU, especially when IDS/IPS is in IDS mode without hardware offload.

Symptoms: WAN throughput drops below ISP speed, controller becomes sluggish, syslog shows softirq/CPU warnings. Mitigation: disable Restrict Access for the IDS/IPS, switch to 'Standard Detection' instead of 'Sensitive', or disable DPI altogether.

UDM-SE and UDM-Pro Max have hardware offload that mostly avoids this; older UDM-Pro hits the wall around 800 Mbps with full IPS.

causes.cause: IDS/IPS Sensitive mode on gigabit WAN
DPI enabled with many concurrent flows
Broken hardware offload after firmware bug

fixSteps.title: Check CPU graph
fixSteps.instruction: In controller > Insights > UDM/UXG, view CPU history.

fixSteps.title: Lower IPS sensitivity
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Internet > Threat Management - set to Standard or Disable.

fixSteps.title: Disable DPI
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Internet > Network Scanners > toggle off Deep Packet Inspection.

fixSteps.title: Test throughput
fixSteps.instruction: Run speed test wired - throughput should rise to ISP rate.

whenToCallPro: If WAN underperforms with all features off, suspect hardware fault and contact UI support.
videoSearchQuery: UDM Pro slow speeds IPS DPI fix

faq.a: Yes - IPS detects attacks in flight. Tradeoff with throughput on lower-end UDMs.
Less so - it has more CPU and better offload than original UDM-Pro.

title: UniFi mesh AP wireless uplink weak/unstable
shortDescription: Wirelessly uplinked AP shows weak signal, low TX rate, or frequent disconnects from its parent.
fullDescription:
U6-Mesh, AC-M, and other wirelessly-uplinked APs show 'Quality: Poor' or low signal % when their backhaul to the parent AP is weak. Throughput halves with each mesh hop, so weak backhaul means very poor client experience.

Move the mesh AP within 30 ft of the parent with line-of-sight, or use the controller's RF Environment to ensure backhaul uses 5 GHz with at least -65 dBm RSSI. If a wired drop is possible, switch to wired uplink - mesh is a last resort.

In controller, set 'Wireless Uplink' priority to a specific known-good parent AP rather than auto-select to prevent flapping.

causes.cause: Mesh AP too far from parent

fixSteps.title: Check link quality
fixSteps.instruction: AP detail > Uplink shows signal dBm and TX rate to parent.

fixSteps.title: Reposition
fixSteps.instruction: Move mesh AP closer (line of sight) to parent until signal is better than -65 dBm.

fixSteps.title: Force best parent
fixSteps.instruction: In AP settings > Wireless Uplink, manually select the strongest parent.

fixSteps.title: Add wired uplink
fixSteps.instruction: Run an ethernet drop and disable wireless uplink for stability.

whenToCallPro: If wired drops are needed in finished walls, hire a low-voltage installer.
videoSearchQuery: UniFi mesh wireless uplink weak fix

faq.q: How much throughput do I lose on mesh?
faq.a: Roughly 50% per hop on shared backhaul.
Yes but each hop halves bandwidth - keep to one hop.

title: High Wi-Fi TX retry rate
shortDescription: Controller flags excessive transmit retries on AP radio - indicates poor RF or interference.
fullDescription:
TX retries are 802.11 retransmissions caused by lost or corrupted frames. A healthy network should sit below 5%; over 15% indicates serious RF problems or struggling clients.

Common culprits: weak/marginal client signal at edge of cell, hidden node interference, microwave/BT/Zigbee on 2.4 GHz, or driver bugs in old IoT clients. UniFi's RF Environment and Insights view show retry % per radio.

Fixes: increase AP density to bring all clients within -65 dBm, set Minimum RSSI to disconnect weak clients, separate IoT to 2.4 GHz only network, and disable lower legacy data rates (1/2/5.5 Mbps).

causes.cause: Clients at edge of cell coverage

symptoms: Slow speed despite good signal bars
Clients near walls slower than near AP

fixSteps.title: Find offenders
fixSteps.instruction: Insights > Radios shows retry % per radio. Click into top offenders.

fixSteps.title: Set Min RSSI
fixSteps.instruction: WiFi network advanced settings > set Minimum RSSI to -75 dBm.

fixSteps.title: Disable low rates
fixSteps.instruction: Disable 802.11b legacy rates (1/2/5.5/11) to push slow IoT off 2.4 GHz.

fixSteps.title: Add APs as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Walk site to map dead zones; add APs to keep all clients above -65 dBm.

whenToCallPro: Site survey by a CWNA professional if retries persist after RF tuning.
videoSearchQuery: UniFi high TX retries fix Wi-Fi

faq.a: Yes - under 5% is fine. Over 15% degrades performance.
Only weak ones get kicked - they roam to closer APs.

title: UniFi switch reports PoE fault on port
shortDescription: Controller marks a switch port with 'PoE Fault' and refuses to power the connected device.
fullDescription:
UniFi PoE switches (USW-Lite-PoE, USW-24-PoE, USW-Pro-Max) detect overcurrent, short, or invalid PD signature and disable PoE on the port. The connected AP/camera doesn't power up. Common triggers: damaged ethernet cable shorting pairs, faulty PD, or exceeding the switch's PoE budget.

In controller > switch ports, the affected port shows red PoE icon. Cycle PoE off/on, and if the fault recurs, swap the cable. Try the suspect device on a different port to isolate cable vs. device.

For passive 24V mode (legacy UAP), make sure the port is configured 24V passive in port profile - feeding 802.3af to a passive-only AP can damage it.

causes.cause: Faulty PD drawing too much current
Wrong PoE mode (24V passive vs af/at)

fixSteps.title: Cycle port PoE
fixSteps.instruction: Toggle PoE off then on for the port from controller.

fixSteps.title: Test cable
fixSteps.instruction: Replace patch cable; if the run is in-wall, test with cable tester.

fixSteps.title: Test PD
fixSteps.instruction: Plug a known-good PD into the same port - if it works, the original PD is bad.

fixSteps.title: Verify PoE mode
fixSteps.instruction: Port profile > PoE - select Auto (af/at) or 24V Passive matching device requirement.

whenToCallPro: If multiple ports show faults simultaneously, suspect switch hardware - RMA via UI.

faq.q: Can a fault damage the switch?
faq.a: Protection circuits prevent damage by disabling the port - that's the fault.
Legacy UAP-AC-Lite/LR and InWall models that don't support 802.3af.

title: UniFi Cloud Key/Controller unreachable
shortDescription: Browser cannot load the UniFi controller and remote login times out.
fullDescription:
When a Cloud Key Gen2/Plus or self-hosted UniFi controller becomes unreachable, all APs continue serving Wi-Fi but cannot be managed. Most causes are software (full disk from camera footage on Gen2+) or power (failed PoE/12V).

For Cloud Key Gen2 with G3 camera storage, a full disk freezes services - SSH in (root/ubnt) and check 'df -h'. Clear oldest recordings via Protect UI or 'rm' in /srv/UNIFI-VIDEO. For self-hosted (Linux), restart the unifi service: 'systemctl restart unifi'.

If hardware is unresponsive, hold reset on Cloud Key for 10 seconds for soft reset (config preserved) or 30 seconds for full factory reset.

causes.cause: Disk full on Cloud Key Gen2 (Protect storage)
Failed eMMC on aging Cloud Key

symptoms: Cloud Key LCD off or blank
APs still serving Wi-Fi but unmanaged

fixSteps.title: Check power
fixSteps.instruction: Verify PoE/12V power LED on Cloud Key. Power-cycle if dark.

fixSteps.title: SSH and check disk
fixSteps.instruction: SSH root@<CK IP> (default root/ubnt) and run 'df -h'. Clear /srv/UNIFI-VIDEO if full.

fixSteps.title: Soft reset
fixSteps.instruction: If still down, hold reset 10s for soft reset preserving config.

whenToCallPro: Suspect hardware fault if soft reset leaves device unresponsive.

faq.a: No - APs run last config; only management is impacted.

faq.q: How do I back up the controller?
faq.a: Settings > System > Backup - download regularly to restore after hardware loss.
